newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes firm amid tight import scene.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes firm amid tight import scene.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes remained scarce Friday amid good refinery demand and poor arbitrage economics with domestic alternatives again benefitting.
Few offers for North Sea or West African crudes were seen, shut out by a narrow Brent/West Texas Intermediate arbitrage at 80 cents a barrel for December and thin European supply.
But rumors persisted that more than three Brents had been placed with U.S. Gulf refiners this week, sold by a European trader who had chartered a ULCC.
Earlier in the week, Brents were sold at Dec WTI plus 50-55 cents cif, but this level was considered unrepeatable.
The only other light sweet crude heard offered was 550,000 barrels of Cusiana for Nov 21-25 from Ecopetrol. Cusiana was valued over last trades reported at Dec WTI plus 10 cents fob.
Elsewhere in the region, Argentine YPF sold Thursday three parcels of Canadon Seco totalling one million barrels at WTI minus $2.39 a barrel fob terminal, to Petrobras.
Traders said foreign sour barrels were also thinly talked although Oriente was seen becoming more competitive with the revision of pricing to West Texas Sour from WTI from Oct 15.
In the U.S. after-market, a full cargo of Dec Brent traded at $24.70 a barrel, up 15 cents from London's IPE close.
Nov/Dec Brent traded at plus 53 cents, within the range seen during the late London session.
